newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Quinn sees 97 gen govt deficit under 1996 target.
newsitem.headline: Quinn sees 97 gen govt deficit under 1996 target.

text.p: Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn said on Monday that the 1997 general government deficit will be lower than the 1996 target of 2.6 percent of GDP.
"The 1997 general government deficit will be significantly lower than the target set in my 1996 budget, which itself was comfortably within the Maastricht guidelines," Quinn said in a statement.

The minister said the 1997 estimates and budget were particularly important since next year's general government deficit will be used to determine which countries participate in economic and monetary union.
"It is essential that Ireland's budgetary performance remains firmly within the parameters set down in the Maastricht Treaty," he said.

Quinn said that over 1996 and 1997 the real increase in current spending will be significantly greater than the target of an annual average rate of two percent for those years set in the policy agreement between the three parties in the ruling coalition government.

"It is however of greater economic importance that over the two years 1996-97, the target set in our policy agreement that the deficit be maintained at a level comfortably within the Maastricht benchmark, will be fully met," he said.
